_comment: The two hazards `<enum>FromString` / `<enum>Values` must survive, in one brand.
`presence` is the MAP form where the Elm IDENT differs from the WIRE STRING for
every token: `always` mints `Ir.token "true"`. `presenceFromString` must case on
"true", not on "always" — casing on the ident would make it disagree with
`toString` for exactly these tokens, silently and in one direction only.
`fallback` adds the FAN-IN: `always` and `yes` both write "true". Nothing rejects
this — `Model.tokenValues` guards token -> one string (each of these has one), and
`guardValuesModule` guards two raw tokens -> one ident (these are two idents). Both
evaluate to the SAME `Ir.token "true"`, so dropping one is lossless; emitting both
would produce a duplicate `case` branch (a compiler warning at best) and a
`always` is shared by BOTH overrides and writes "true" in each, so the brand-wide
token pool mints it once — asking it to write two strings is a separate hard error
